create.name: Vedanta Center of Atlanta
create.bio:
The Vedanta Center of Atlanta is a small centre of the Ramakrishna–Vivekananda tradition in Tucker, on the north-east edge of Atlanta, Georgia. It grew from classes begun in the 1980s by Swami Yogeshananda, a monk of the Ramakrishna Order who came to bring Vedanta to the American South; the group met in rented rooms under the name The Eternal Quest until friends helped buy a house in Tucker, and a chapel was added in 2006. Since then it has been guided by ministers linked with the Vedanta Society of Southern California, and visiting swamis of the order now give most of its talks.

The centre teaches Vedanta and Hindu devotion in the light of Sri Ramakrishna, his wife and spiritual partner Sri Sarada Devi, and his disciples Swami Vivekananda and Swami Brahmananda. Its programme includes Sunday talks, weekday classes on texts such as the Katha Upanishad and the Yoga Sutras, a weekly group reading of the life of Ramakrishna, evening arati, Ram Naam chanting, yoga and occasional retreats, held at the chapel and on Zoom. Nothing is charged for any of it. The YouTube channel, running since 2019, keeps recordings of these talks and classes, and the centre also has a bookshop and lending library.

free_resources.title: Talks, Classes and Worship
free_resources.description: The centre's calendar of Sunday talks, weekday study classes, evening arati, chanting and yoga, at the chapel or on Zoom. All are free and open to anyone.

free_resources.title: Audio and Video Archive
free_resources.description: A dated list of recorded talks and class series, recent years on video and earlier years as audio, with speakers' notes where available.

free_resources.title: Prayers, Chants and Music
free_resources.description: Texts and recordings of prayers and chants used at the centre, including a hymn to Ramakrishna by Swami Vivekananda.
